'''Curtis Lynea Meinert''' (June 30, 1934 – June 13, 2023) was an American clinical trialist. He was a professor of epidemiology and biostatistics at [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health]].

== Life ==
Meinert was born on June 30, 1934, on a farm outside [[Sleepy Eye, Minnesota]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Obituary for Curtis Lynea Meinert at Ruck Towson Funeral Home, Inc. |url=https://www.ruckfuneral.com/obituary/curtis-meinert?lud=D367FE46934B93239B5D0C8421C485C9 |access-date=2023-06-16 |website=www.ruckfuneral.com |language=en}}</ref> His parents were Mabel Eleanor Christensen and Arthur August Edward Meinert.<ref name=":2" /> He was raised in rural [[Minnesota]].<ref name=":0" /> He completed a B.A. in psychology from the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1956.<ref name=":2" /> He earned a doctor of philosophy in statistics at University of Minnesota in 1964.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.epi.umn.edu/cvdepi/bio-sketch/meinert-curtis/|title=Meinert, Curtis « Heart Attack Prevention|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Virtual International Authority File|url=https://viaf.org/viaf/48169060/|access-date=2020-12-06|website=VIAF}}</ref> His dissertation was titled ''Quantitation of the isotope displacement of immunoassay of insulin''.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 1965|title=News and Notices|journal=The Annals of Mathematical Statistics|volume=36|issue=2|pages=737–744|jstor=2238184|doi=10.1214/aoms/1177700189|doi-access=free}}</ref> His advisor was [[Richard B. McHugh]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=781OAQAAMAAJ|title=Register of Ph. D. Degrees Conferred by the University of Minnesota|date=1956|publisher=University of Minnesota|pages=177|language=en}}</ref>

Meinert was the head of a clinical trial coordinating center at [[University of Maryland]]. Meinert researched randomized clinical trials for AIDS, cardiovascular diseases, and asthma.<ref name=":0" /> He was a professor of epidemiology and biostatistics and the inaugural director of the Center for Clinical Trials at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jhsph.edu/faculty/directory/profile/469/curtis-meinert|title=Curtis Meinert - Faculty Directory|last=Health|first=JH Bloomberg School of Public|website=Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health|language=en|access-date=2019-02-27}}</ref> 

In 1979, Meinert was elected a fellow of the [[American College of Epidemiology]]. In 1995, he was elected [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He was a 2001 Fellow of the [[American Heart Association]]. In 2006, he was elected a fellow of the [[Society for Clinical Trials]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2005, Johns Hopkins University established the professorship, Curtis L. Meinert Professor of Clinical Trials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://professorships.jhu.edu/professorship/curtis-l-meinert-professorship-in-clinical-trials/|title=Curtis L. Meinert Professorship in Clinical Trials|last1=Donor|first1=Office of|last2=Baltimore|first2=Volunteer Engagement 3400 North Charles Street|website=Named Deanships, Directorships, and Professorships|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-27|last3=Development|first3=MD 21218 410-516-8631|last4=Relations|first4=Alumni|date=23 June 2016 }}</ref>

Meinert married Susan J. Matson on June 22, 1957. They had three daughters. He died on June 13, 2023, at the age of 88.<ref name=":2" />
